title: Characterizing Power Management Opportunities for LLMs in the Cloud
problem: Datacenter power capacity is rapidly becoming a critical bottleneck for GPU compute resources as large language model sizes increase and their datacenter demand grows. Cloud providers lack clear characterization of power consumption patterns and optimization opportunities for LLM workloads.
motivation: With LLMs saturating datacenter power budgets and cloud providers planning substantial capacity expansion, understanding power management opportunities is essential for sustainable scaling of AI infrastructure.
method: The paper measures the electricity use and heat generated by large language models when running on GPUs (graphics processors) in datacenters, covering both inference (using existing models) and training (building new ones). It then reviews the power management techniques datacenters currently use and identifies specific opportunities to reduce how much electricity these models consume.
key_novelty: By studying large language models specifically in cloud datacenters, it identifies which power optimizations would have the greatest impact.
contributions: Characterization of power consumption patterns for LLM inference and training on datacenter GPUs
Identification of power management optimization opportunities for LLM workloads
Analysis of how power constraints limit datacenter scaling for LLM capacity
primary_theme: Power management optimization for cloud LLMs
